Showing sound

design spec·euterpe and scriptorium·before v0.1.0

Every Euterpe object can show itself. display(x) draws its default view with a player, a method such as x.spectrum() returns another view, and listen(x) returns the player alone. The objects follow IPython's rich-display protocol, so the same line works in Jupyter and in a scriptorium book, and the book's hand-written matplotlib figures become one call each.

01What this delivers

  • A Clip: a unit rendered for a known number of seconds. Units that end on their own (an envelope, a pluck) report their duration, so most sounds need no seconds at all.
  • A euterpe.view package with six views for layer 1 (waveform, spectrum, spectrogram, level, filter response, shaper curve) and the player, plus row() to put views side by side. Every view accepts several sources with labels, because most of the book's figures compare sounds.
  • One contract, IPython's _repr_mimebundle_, that layers 2 to 4 reuse: a chord, a scale and a score will be views with the same shape, an SVG drawing plus audio.
  • Scriptorium support for display() and for a rich last expression, generic and without any Euterpe import.
  • The book migrated to it before v0.1.0. Counted in book/chapters/ on 2026-10-26:
31
matplotlib figures in the book today

02Decisions

maintainer marks a call made in the brainstorm; agent marks one the spec's author made, open to change.

DecisionChoiceWhyBy
Entry pointdisplay(x) shows the default view of any Euterpe object; methods return other views; listen(x) gives the player only.One verb to see a thing, the one Jupyter users already know.maintainer
ProtocolIPython's rich display: objects implement _repr_mimebundle_. Euterpe does not import IPython.Works in Jupyter, nbconvert and VS Code with no glue, and gives scriptorium a published contract to read.maintainer
Where it runsThe same objects in Jupyter and in the book. Scriptorium learns display() and the last expression.The book's code is code a reader can paste into a notebook.maintainer
Caption and idCarried by the object as display metadata (caption=, id= on every view, or display(x, metadata=...)). A code block's attributes are the fallback.Keeps the figure's identity next to the call that makes it.maintainer
Scope in timeBuilt and the book migrated before v0.1.0. Views for theory and score are designed here and built with their layers.v0.1.0 should ship the API the book teaches.maintainer
DurationA Unit is an endless recipe; unit.take(seconds) makes a Clip. Units that end report duration; without one, a view renders 1 s and says so on the drawing.Most book sounds end on their own; the rest get a visible default, not a silent one.agent
Where files get writtenThe cell prints the bundle; scriptorium's parent process writes the SVG and MP3 under build/.The freeze cache then holds everything needed to rebuild a page, and the cell has no side effects.agent
Last expressionScriptorium shows a cell's last expression only when it has a rich repr.Existing books whose last line returns a plain value keep their output unchanged.agent
ComparisonViews take several sources: spectrum(a, b, labels=["dry", "low-pass"]). a.spectrum() is the one-source shorthand.Most of the book's figures overlay or compare sounds: four waves, three low-passes, noise colours.agent
Players in the bookThe 104 players stay player-only (listen). display, with its drawing, is used where the text talks about the shape.A waveform above every player would double the page length without teaching more.agent
Dependencymatplotlib as an optional extra, euterpe[view], imported lazily.Synthesis and the CLI do not need it; the error names the extra to install.agent

03How it fits

04Units, clips and duration

tone = (Sine(440) * 0.5).take(2.0)   # a Clip of 2 s
display(tone)                         # waveform and player
display(tone.spectrum())              # spectrum
listen(tone)                          # player only
display(Pluck(220))                    # no seconds: Pluck knows when it dies
  • Unit.take(seconds=None) -> Clip renders from a reset unit, the way render does today. With no seconds it uses duration, and 1 s when that is None. render stays and returns the array.
  • Unit.duration -> float | None is the time after which the output stays below -60 dBFS. An ADSR reports gate plus release; a Pluck computes it from its damping; a product or gain takes the shortest finite factor; a mix takes the longest, and is None if any input is; delays and reverbs add their tail to their input's. Each unit's docstring says how it computes it.
  • A Clip holds float32 samples and the rate, exposes seconds and __array__ so NumPy code keeps working, and has the view methods. euterpe.io.read keeps returning (samples, rate); Clip.read(path) is new.
  • When a view used the 1 s default, its drawing says "1 s (default)" in the corner, so a reader never mistakes the default for a choice.

05Views

A view is a small object: what to draw, from which sources, with which options, plus its caption and id. It draws nothing until a host asks for its bundle. Every view lives in euterpe.view as a function taking one or more sources; the methods on Clip and Unit are one-source shorthands. A source may be a unit or a clip: a unit is taken first.

from euterpe.view import spectrum, waveform, row

display(spectrum(Sine(220), Saw(220), Square(220), Triangle(220),
                 labels=["sine", "saw", "square", "triangle"], upto=6000,
                 caption="The spectra of the four waves at 220 Hz, up to 6 kHz", id="fig-four-spectra"))

row(waveform(dry, wet, span=(0, 0.08)), level(dry, wet), caption="...")   # left and right panels

All views share one house style (section 06) in euterpe/view/style.py. The same drawing code feeds euterpe inspect, which writes PNGs for agents, so the CLI and the book never draw the same thing two ways.

06The look

The views have to read as plates in a book about music, not as a plotting library's defaults. The reference is the engraved figures of nineteenth-century acoustics, such as Helmholtz's plates, and music engraving: fine ink lines on white paper, italic serif labels written beside what they name, and no box around anything. Every figure in this section was rendered by matplotlib from the real Euterpe units with a draft of the style that becomes euterpe/view/style.py; the future views were drawn with the same code and sample music.

Inks and type

ink#1e2430lines, text, staff
prussian#1f5f8bfirst series, spectrogram ink
madder#b0361fwhat the text points at
verdigris#2f7d6dthird series
ochre#b8862bfourth series
rule#9aa0a8hairlines, the reference series
  • Type is the book's own serif, Source Serif 4: axis labels and annotations in italic, numbers upright. Glyphs are stored as paths in the SVG, because a figure loaded as an image cannot use the page's fonts; the caption carries the text for screen readers. Noto Music supplies ♯, ♭ and the clefs.
  • Only the left and bottom axes, offset from the data by 4 pt, ticks outward. No grid, no legend box: each series is named in its own ink beside its line.
  • Madder is reserved for what the paragraph is talking about: the magnified window, the resonant peak, the dominant chord. A figure has at most one madder thing.
  • The signature: every frequency axis is also a keyboard. Spectra and responses carry an octave ruler with each A named; spectrograms are log-frequency with a piano along the edge.
  • Spectrograms are ink on paper (white is silence, blue-black is loud) and are stored as an image inside the SVG, so a 3 s spectrogram weighs about 0.7 MB instead of hundreds.

07The display contract

A view's _repr_mimebundle_(include=None, exclude=None) returns (data, metadata):

KeyContentRead by
image/svg+xmlThe drawing, deterministic: no date, fonts as text.scriptorium, Jupyter when HTML is excluded
audio/mpegThe MP3, base64. Present on the default view and the player.scriptorium
text/htmlThe SVG inline and an <audio controls> with a data URI.Jupyter, VS Code, nbconvert
text/plainA one-line summary: Clip(2.0 s, peak -6.0 dBFS).terminals, the REPL
metadata caption, idFrom caption= and id=, or from display(x, metadata=...), which wins.scriptorium

Every Euterpe object that can be shown also implements _repr_mimebundle_ by delegating to its default view, which is what makes display(x) work on a unit or a clip. Layers 2 to 4 add objects, not keys: a chord's bundle has the same four keys.

08Scriptorium

Scriptorium learns the bundle, not Euterpe. The change is in its Python driver and in the code that splices a block's output.

  1. The driver defines display(*objs, metadata=None) as a builtin unless the block imports IPython's. For each object it takes _repr_mimebundle_, or the single _repr_*_ methods, and prints the bundle as JSON between sentinels.
  2. After the block runs, if its last statement is an expression whose value has a rich repr, the driver displays it, as Jupyter does. A plain value prints nothing, as today.
  3. The parent splits stdout into Markdown and bundles. For a bundle it prefers, in order: text/markdown (spliced); an image (image/svg+xml, image/png) and audio (audio/mpeg, audio/wav) written under the book's build/img and build/audio, named by caption slug and content hash as Euterpe's helpers do today; text/html as raw HTML; text/plain as output code.
  4. An image with audio becomes one figure: the image, the player below it, one caption, one number. Its id takes the fig- prefix; audio alone keeps aud-.
  5. A block's caption= and id= attributes apply when the block displays exactly one bundle that carries none. With several bundles the build warns.
  6. The freeze cache stores the bundles with stdout, so a frozen build (marginalia) writes the files again without running Python.

This lands as a scriptorium release; Euterpe's book pins it.

09The book's figures

A typical cell today, from chapter 1:

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 2.5))
ax.plot(ms, x)
ax.set_xlabel("time (ms)")
ax.set_ylabel("pressure (full scale = 1)")
ax.axhline(0, color="grey", linewidth=0.5)
show(fig, "The first 5 ms of the 440 Hz sine: a little over two cycles")

After:

(Sine(440.0) * 0.5).waveform(span=(0, 0.005),
    caption="The first 5 ms of the 440 Hz sine: a little over two cycles")
  • Captions and ids do not change, and neither does the chapter text. The migration changes code and pictures only.
  • The four hand-drawn figures plot functions, not sounds: chapter 1's aliasing and polyBLEP, chapter 2's piano keys and its loudness curve. They wrap their matplotlib figure in euterpe.view.figure(fig, caption=...), which applies the house style and the same contract.
  • listen(unit, seconds, caption) becomes listen(unit, caption=...), or listen(unit.take(seconds), caption=...) when the text names a length. euterpe.book.show and listen are removed once no chapter uses them; gain_db stays.
  • A cell's code gets shorter: the reader sees the sound and the view, not the axes.

10Theory and score views

Designed now so layers 2 to 4 add objects without changing the contract. None of these are built in this work.

Objectdisplay(x)Other views
PitchThe note on a staff, with its player..keyboard(): the key on a piano; .spectrum() through an instrument.
IntervalTwo notes on a staff, quality and number written under them, with its player..keyboard()
ChordThe chord on a staff, symbol and Roman numeral under it, with its player..keyboard(), .spectrum(), .voicing() in staff and roll
Scale, KeyThe scale on a staff with degrees, with its player..keyboard(), .circle() on the circle of fifths
InstrumentA short phrase through it, waveform and player..spectrum(pitch), .registers()
ScoreThe engraved score, paged, with its player..roll() (piano roll per part), .chroma(), .level(), .part(name)

The engraving engine is chosen with layer 3: drawing the staff in SVG ourselves, or writing MusicXML and rendering it with an existing engraver. The contract holds either way: the bundle carries an SVG.

11Delivery

Scriptorium: display support

Driver builtin, last expression, bundle splicing, figure with player, freeze cache. Issue, PR, release.

Euterpe: clips and duration

Clip, take, duration on every unit, with tests per unit.

Euterpe: views

euterpe.view: the six views, the player, row, figure, the house style, the bundle, euterpe[view].

The book, chapter by chapter

One PR for chapters 1 to 8. Each chapter is checked at 390 px and at desktop width against the published page before merge.

Listening pass, then v0.1.0

The maintainer listens to the migrated Part I; the tag follows.

12Testing

  • Duration: for every unit, render past duration and check the output stays below -60 dBFS after it; units without an end report None.
  • Views: each view on a known source gives an SVG with its axis labels as text, the same bytes twice, and a bundle with the keys of section 07.
  • Scriptorium: a block with display, a block ending in a rich expression, a block ending in a plain value (unchanged output), block attributes, several bundles, and a frozen rebuild that recreates the files.
  • The book: it builds from scratch, it has 31 figures and 104 players, the captions are the same set as before, and no page is wider than 390 px.
  • A notebook test: execute a small notebook with nbconvert and check the output cells carry text/html with an <svg and an <audio.

13Non-goals

  • Interactive widgets (sliders, live playback) in Jupyter.
  • A dark theme for the views: they are plates on white paper in both of the book's themes.
  • Any theory or score view: section 10 and the gallery fix their shape only.
  • Changing chapter text, captions or the sounds the book plays.

14Open questions

  • Players stay player-only in the book (decision table). If you want a waveform above some of them, name the chapters.
  • The default view's 50 ms threshold between one panel and two is a guess, to tune on the book's sounds.
